decision.text: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py, replace run_instrument's body: argv = [os.path.join(CAIRN_ROOT, 'bin', 'cairn'), 'test', '--exec', command, '--timeout', str(timeout_s)]; subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s + 120). The timeout N is the function's own timeout_s argument (default _TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600, or the criterion's declared timeout_s); the +120 only bounds the tester's snapshot and teardown. --exec has no structured output: it passes the command's stdout, stderr and exit code through unchanged, so the record is built exactly as before — command (the instrument as given), exit (returncode), timed_out False, timeout_s, seconds (wall time measured here), tail (_tail of stdout + stderr). Two tester lines on stderr are read by prefix: exit 124 with a line starting 'cairn test --exec: timed out after' sets exit None and timed_out True; exit 2 with a line starting 'cairn test --exec: refused' adds seal_refused = that line and keeps exit 2. Nothing else is forked in either case — never a fallback to bash -c. The existing TimeoutExpired and OSError arms stay as they are.
